> **Revision 2 (force-pushed once, minutes after the draft opened, no external reviews yet).** Restructured after an internal review: this PR is now only the bounded backend calls, the host-slot quarantine, their metrics and docs. Changes from revision 1: per-slot pin counts instead of a pinned set (overlapping pins from a KV read and its sidecar read, or a whole-operation write over its per-batch writes, were released by the first unpin); the KV-derived sidecar read is skipped after a KV miss; a backend-raised `TimeoutError` is classified as an error, not as our deadline (same class on Python 3.11+); calls issued after a stop request return the miss without being dispatched; the one-caller-per-kind invariant is enforced; pools derived from a side pool are pinned explicitly; the refusal state is reported once as an ERROR; defaults lowered to 5 / 20 / 60 s; the unified page-envelope pool's `clear()` bounds its lease wait; the guard is an instance member.
>
> **Revision 3 (additional commit, after a second internal review).** The one-caller rule had a second QUERY caller: the PD-decode scheduler thread probes L3 through `query_storage_hit_length` while the prefetch worker's query for the previous request may be in flight, so under `--enable-decode-hicache` the enforcement would have raised out of the scheduler loop. Scheduler-thread probes (that probe and PP0's ticket submission) now run on their own `PROBE` lane with the query deadline, and `query_storage_hit_length` turns any guard error into a miss. Also: the lane is freed before the orphan's spans are pinned (a pin failure can no longer leave a kind permanently busy), the deadline keys are validated before `attach_storage_backend` has any side effect, and the unified page-envelope wording below is corrected.

## Motivation

The HiCache controller talks to the L3 storage backend from single worker threads (`prefetch_thread_func`, `prefetch_io_aux_func`, `backup_thread_func`) and the backend contract has no deadline. One backend call that never returns on one rank therefore wedges the whole prefetch/backup pipeline on **every** rank: the peer ranks block in the MIN collectives behind it (`_sync_prefetch_hit_query`, `_reduce_prefetch_ack`) and every later operation queues behind the stuck one. Under `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout` every later L3-hit request is deadline-cut and recomputed forever (plus a re-upload storm), under `wait_complete` every >= `prefetch_threshold` prompt hangs, and `/health` stays green because short prompts still run. #43550 made a *raising* backend call survivable; a *hanging* one (stuck RPC, slow `scandir`, dead metadata server) reproduces number for number.

Measured on a TP2 file-backend lane with one injected fault (Qwen2.5-1.5B, buffer_only, write_through; 16 seeded 6-8k prefixes, replay #1, then 8 healthy L3-hit requests at +10 s and 6 more at +2 min, then `/flush_cache`), this PR with its default bounds (5 / 20 / 60 s):

| fault | policy | before (main) | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_get` hangs on rank 1 | timeout | #1 2.92 s cached 0; **all 14 later L3-hit requests cached 0** (2.5-3.0 s each) forever; `/flush_cache` kills both schedulers | #1 2.92 s cached 0 (deadline cut); the 8 requests at +10 s are still cut (the GET lane is blocked until the 20 s bound expires); **the 6 at +2 min get full hits** (0.15-0.30 s); flush 200, alive |
| `batch_get` hangs on rank 1 | wait_complete | #1 **stalls > 150 s, all 14 later requests stall** | #1 20.09 s cached 0 (= GET bound + recompute); the 8 at +10 s wait behind the hung read and get **full hits at 10.2-10.4 s**; the 6 at +2 min full hits in 0.1-0.3 s; flush 200 |
| `batch_exists` raises on rank 0 | timeout | the faulted and every later >= 256-token request pays +1.0-1.2 s with cached 0 (query thread dead, peer in gloo); flush 200 then dead | only the faulted request misses (0.05 s TTFT, recompute); **13/13 others full hits**; flush 200 |
| `batch_exists` raises on rank 0 | wait_complete | every later >= 256-token prompt **stalls** | same as timeout: one miss, 13/13 full hits; flush 200 |

With tighter bounds (2 / 5 / 10 s, same guard, revision-1 build) the 8 requests at +10 s got full hits in all four scenarios as well; the default GET bound trades that head-of-line window for not cutting legitimately slow transfers.

## Modifications

**1. Bounded backend calls (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage_call_guard.py`, new).** `StorageCallGuard.run()` executes one backend call on a per-kind daemon worker (`hicache-storage-{query,probe,get,set}`) while the controller thread waits with a deadline. On timeout *or* exception it logs a rate-limited WARNING (kind, op, key count), counts it, and returns the controller's own miss shape, so every per-batch `PrefetchAck` / hit count / backup ack is still produced and the peers' MIN reduces stay balanced:

| call site | miss shape |
|---|---|
| `_storage_hit_query` (`batch_exists`, hybrid `batch_exists_v2`) | `0` / `PoolTransferResult.empty()` |
| `_page_transfer_kv_batch` (`page_get_func`, KV-derived `batch_get_v2`, skipped after a KV miss), hybrid `_page_transfer_sidecar` (`batch_get_v2`) | `0` pages / all-`False` per transfer (`pool_transfer_misses`) |
| `_page_backup` (`page_set_func`), hybrid `_page_backup_with_stable_layout` (`batch_set_v2`) | `False` / all-`False` |

Each kind has exactly one calling thread, which the guard enforces: the controller's query, transfer and backup workers for `QUERY` / `GET` / `SET`, and the scheduler thread for `PROBE`, the existence probes it issues itself (the PD-decode hit probe in `query_storage_hit_length`, PP0's ticket submission in `submit_prefetch`), which share `storage_query_timeout_s` and therefore wait up to it on the scheduler thread. A probe may overlap the prefetch worker's query, hence the separate lane. Calls of one kind run one at a time unless the earlier one was orphaned. Deadlines come from `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config` keys `storage_query_timeout_s` / `storage_get_timeout_s` / `storage_set_timeout_s` (popped before the backend sees the config; `0`/`null` disables; defaults **5 / 20 / 60 s** per batch call of up to 128 pages, i.e. one to two orders of magnitude above the healthy tails measured on remote backends). A backend-raised `TimeoutError` counts as an error, not as our deadline. Once a stop request (reset / detach) is posted, the call in flight gets a 5 s grace and later calls return the miss without being dispatched, so the controller threads stay joinable. Backend classes are untouched.

**2. Orphan ownership.** A timed-out call is not cancelled; it keeps running on its now-orphaned worker and a fresh worker serves the next call. Because zero-copy `batch_get_v1/v2` write straight into host pool rows and `batch_set*` read them, those rows must not be reused while the orphan is alive. Before publishing the miss the guard quarantines the spans the call touches (`HostSpan`: the KV batch span in the anchor pool, each side pool's `host_indices` in the pool that allocated them, the KV span for KV-derived pools) via a new allocator-level `HostSlotQuarantine` (`pool_host/base.py`) wired into `HostKVCache.free/clear`, `LogicalHostPool`, `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool`, `MambaPoolHost` and the unified page-envelope backing. Pins are counted per slot. The owner keeps freeing as usual (ack drain, hybrid discard, abort, staging release, L2 eviction, `/flush_cache` clear); the pinned part is held instead of returned to the free list and comes back when the orphan's done-callback calls `release_quarantine`. The hybrid worker also holds `mem_pool_host.layout_lease()` around the call so an orphan keeps the unified layout pinned; a `clear()` of that pool now bounds its wait for such a lease (10 s) and raises instead of blocking the scheduler forever. After `max_orphans` (4) hung calls of one kind, new calls of that kind return the miss immediately; that state is reported once as an ERROR, and the pinned-memory ceiling is `max_orphans` x 128 pages per kind and rank.

**3. Observability.** `sglang:hicache_storage_call_timeouts_total{kind}`, `sglang:hicache_storage_call_errors_total{kind}` (raised or refused) and the gauge `sglang:hicache_storage_orphaned_calls{kind}` in `StorageMetricsCollector`, fed from the guard on the existing per-tick `log_storage_metrics` path. Docs: a "Bounding Storage Backend Calls" subsection in `hicache_best_practices.mdx`.

Three existing unit fixtures that build bare controllers (`test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py`, `test_pp_prefetch_ticket.py`, `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`) gain one line each for the new call hook.

Points for reviewers:
- **Default bounds.** Under `wait_complete` the GET bound is the TTFT of every request queued behind one hung read (measured 10.2-10.4 s with the 20 s default); under `timeout` those requests are deadline-cut until the bound expires. 5 / 20 / 60 s keeps >= 15x headroom over the measured healthy tails; `wait_complete` users with a fast backend can set `storage_get_timeout_s` to ~10x their p99.
- **Orphan ownership** is implemented in the allocators rather than by making backends cancellable, so it covers every backend without per-backend work; the cost is host memory pinned for as long as a hung call lives (bounded by `max_orphans`) and a few lines in each slot-list allocator.
- **Unified page-envelope (mori) pool.** An orphan holds a layout lease; compaction and `clear()` wait for it. Keeping quarantined pages immovable and not waiting for abandoned leases is part of the follow-up PR (#44348), which removes that outcome.
- **A worker that cannot be joined** (bound disabled, or a thread stuck in a gloo collective because its peer died) still makes `reset()` raise exactly as on main; the follow-up PR turns that into a reported, rank-agreed degradation.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward or to what a successful transfer writes. A timed-out or failed call is published as a miss (recompute), never as data.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No-fault control on the same lane (16 seeded prefixes replayed, `timeout` policy): per-request TTFT within +-0.03 s of main and identical hit token counts; the only added per-call work is one queue hand-off to the worker thread (tens of microseconds against a 128-page batch). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 ```
 
+### Bounding Storage Backend Calls
+
+Every storage backend call made by the HiCache controller runs under a deadline. A call that misses it is treated as an ordinary miss (0 hits, 0 transferred pages, or a failed backup) and the prefetch/backup pipeline keeps flowing, instead of one stuck call wedging the worker thread, its TP peers, and any later `/flush_cache` (on the unified page-envelope host pool a flush issued while an orphaned call still holds its layout lease gives up after 10 s and, as before, exits the scheduler). The timed-out call keeps running on an orphaned worker and the host memory it may still touch stays quarantined until it returns; `sglang:hicache_storage_call_timeouts_total`, `sglang:hicache_storage_call_errors_total`, and `sglang:hicache_storage_orphaned_calls` report it.
+
+```bash Command
+--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"storage_query_timeout_s": 5, "storage_get_timeout_s": 20, "storage_set_timeout_s": 60}'
+```
+
+The values above are the defaults, in seconds per batch call (one existence query / page read / page write covers up to 128 pages, not a whole request); `0` or `null` disables the bound for that kind. Keep them well above the backend's healthy tail latency (about 10x its p99 is a good start): a call that is merely slow is cut and recomputed, and under `wait_complete` every request queued behind a hung call waits until its bound expires. At most 4 hung calls per kind are kept alive per rank; their host memory (4 x 128 pages per kind) stays pinned until they return, and further calls of that kind are refused as misses in the meantime.

+"""Deadline-bounded execution of HiCache storage-backend calls.
+
+The HiCache controller talks to the L3 backend from single worker threads, and a
+backend call that never returns wedges that thread: the peer ranks block in the
+MIN collectives behind it, every later prefetch or backup queues behind it, and a
+``reset()`` can no longer join the thread. The guard runs each backend call on a
+per-kind worker and waits with a deadline. A call that misses it is published as
+the controller's ordinary miss; the worker that still runs it is orphaned and a
+fresh worker serves the next call. The host slots an orphaned call may still
+read or write stay quarantined in their pool until the call returns, so a late
+completion can never land in memory that was handed to another operation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import concurrent.futures
+import logging
+import math
+import threading
+import time
+from enum import Enum
+from queue import Queue
+from typing import Any, Callable, Optional, Sequence, TypeVar
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+# Granularity at which a waiting controller thread re-checks the stop event.
+_STOP_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 0.5
+# How long a stop request (reset / detach) lets the call already in flight
+# finish before orphaning it; below the controller's 10 s thread join so the
+# thread stays joinable, long enough that a detach rarely closes a backend
+# under a live call. Calls issued after the stop are not dispatched at all.
+_STOP_GRACE_S = 5.0
+# Minimum spacing between WARNING lines per call kind.
+_WARN_INTERVAL_S = 5.0
+
+
+class StorageCallKind(Enum):
+    # Existence queries issued by the prefetch worker.
+    QUERY = "query"
+    # Existence probes issued by the scheduler thread (the PD-decode hit probe,
+    # PP0's ticket submission), which may overlap a QUERY; same deadline key.
+    PROBE = "probe"
+    GET = "get"
+    SET = "set"
+
+
+_EXTRA_CONFIG_KEYS = {
+    StorageCallKind.QUERY: "storage_query_timeout_s",
+    StorageCallKind.GET: "storage_get_timeout_s",
+    StorageCallKind.SET: "storage_set_timeout_s",
+}
+
+
+class StorageCallTimeouts(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """Deadline in seconds for one backend call of each kind; None disables it.
+
+    Each call covers one STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE-page batch. The defaults sit one to
+    two orders of magnitude above the healthy tails measured on remote backends
+    (ms-scale queries, up to about a second per batch) while keeping the wait of
+    anything queued behind a hung call short.
+    """
+
+    query_s: Optional[float] = 5.0
+    get_s: Optional[float] = 20.0
+    set_s: Optional[float] = 60.0
+    # Orphaned (timed-out, still running) calls tolerated per kind before new
+    # calls of that kind are refused as misses. Arbitrary. It also bounds the
+    # host memory a hanging backend can pin: max_orphans batches of
+    # STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE pages per kind and rank.
+    max_orphans: int = 4
+
+    @classmethod
+    def disabled(cls) -> StorageCallTimeouts:
+        return cls(query_s=None, get_s=None, set_s=None)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def pop_from_extra_config(
+        cls, extra_config: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
+    ) -> StorageCallTimeouts:
+        """Take the ``storage_*_timeout_s`` keys (0 or null disables) out of
+        ``--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config`` so backends never see them."""
+        if not extra_config:
+            return cls()
+        values: dict[str, Optional[float]] = {}
+        for kind, key in _EXTRA_CONFIG_KEYS.items():
+            if key not in extra_config:
+                continue
+            raw = extra_config.pop(key)
+            if raw is not None and (
+                isinstance(raw, bool)
+                or not isinstance(raw, (int, float))
+                or not math.isfinite(raw)
+                or raw < 0
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{key} must be a finite number of seconds >= 0, got {raw!r}"
+                )
+            values[f"{kind.value}_s"] = None if not raw else float(raw)
+        return cls(**values)
+
+    def for_kind(self, kind: StorageCallKind) -> Optional[float]:
+        if kind in (StorageCallKind.QUERY, StorageCallKind.PROBE):
+            return self.query_s
+        if kind is StorageCallKind.GET:
+            return self.get_s
+        return self.set_s
+

+    """Host slots a backend call reads or writes; ``pool`` owns their quarantine."""

+    """Per-kind counts: timeouts and errors since the previous snapshot,

+    errors: dict[str, int]
+    orphaned: dict[str, int]
+
+
+class _GuardTimeout(Exception):
+    """The guard's own deadline expired (never a backend-raised TimeoutError)."""
+

+class _Worker:
+    def __init__(self, kind: StorageCallKind):
+        self.inbox: Queue = Queue()
+        self.orphaned = False
+        self.thread = threading.Thread(
+            target=self._loop, name=f"hicache-storage-{kind.value}", daemon=True
+        )
+        self.thread.start()
+
+    def _loop(self) -> None:
+        while True:
+            job = self.inbox.get()
+            if job is None:
+                return
+            fn, future = job
+            try:
+                result = fn()
+            except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - delivered to the caller
+                future.set_exception(error)
+            else:
+                future.set_result(result)
+            if self.orphaned:
+                return
+
+
+class _Orphan:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        kind: StorageCallKind,
+        spans: Sequence[HostSpan],
+        op: str,
+        started_at: float,
+    ):
+        self.kind = kind
+        self.spans = spans
+        self.op = op
+        self.started_at = started_at
+
+
+class _Lane:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.worker: Optional[_Worker] = None
+        # True while a call is dispatched and not yet returned or orphaned.
+        self.busy = False
+        self.next_orphan_id = 0
+        self.orphans: dict[int, _Orphan] = {}
+        self.refusing = False
+        self.timeouts = 0
+        self.errors = 0
+        self.last_warn_at = -_WARN_INTERVAL_S
+        self.suppressed_warnings = 0
+
+
+class StorageCallGuard:
+    """Runs backend calls under per-kind deadlines; see the module docstring.
+
+    Each kind has exactly one calling thread (the controller's query, transfer
+    and backup workers for QUERY, GET and SET; the scheduler thread for PROBE),
+    so calls of one kind run strictly one at a time unless the one in flight
+    was orphaned. A second caller on a kind is a programming error and raises.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        timeouts: StorageCallTimeouts,
+        *,
+        label: str = "",
+        stop_event: Optional[threading.Event] = None,
+    ):
+        self.timeouts = timeouts
+        self._label = label
+        self._stop_event = stop_event
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._lanes = {kind: _Lane() for kind in StorageCallKind}
+
+    def run(
+        self,
+        kind: StorageCallKind,
+        fn: Callable[[], T],
+        *,
+        miss: Callable[[], T],
+        op: str,
+        num_keys: int,
+        spans: Optional[Callable[[], Sequence[HostSpan]]] = None,
+        lease: Optional[Callable[[], Any]] = None,
+    ) -> T:
+        """Call ``fn`` with the deadline of ``kind``.
+
+        On timeout or exception the result is ``miss()``, the controller's own
+        shape for "nothing came back"; ``spans()`` names the host slots a timed
+        out call keeps touching so they can be quarantined until it returns.
+        ``lease()`` is a context manager the worker holds around the call so an
+        orphan keeps pinning the host layout its indices were resolved against.
+        """
+        timeout = self.timeouts.for_kind(kind)
+        if timeout is None:
+            return fn()
+        if self._stop_event is not None and self._stop_event.is_set():
+            # Shutting down: the result is discarded anyway, and dispatching
+            # would hand every queued call another grace period.
+            return miss()
+        if lease is not None:
+            unleased_fn = fn
+
+            def fn():
+                with lease():
+                    return unleased_fn()
+
+        lane = self._lanes[kind]
+        started_at = time.monotonic()
+        with self._lock:
+            if lane.busy:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"HiCache storage {kind.value} calls must come from one thread; "
+                    f"{op} was issued while another call is in flight"
+                )
+            pending_orphans = len(lane.orphans)
+            refused = (
+                lane.worker is None and pending_orphans >= self.timeouts.max_orphans
+            )
+            if refused:
+                lane.errors += 1
+                first_refusal = not lane.refusing
+                lane.refusing = True
+            else:
+                if lane.worker is None:
+                    lane.worker = _Worker(kind)
+                worker = lane.worker
+                future: concurrent.futures.Future = concurrent.futures.Future()
+                lane.busy = True
+                worker.inbox.put((fn, future))
+        if refused:
+            if first_refusal:
+                logger.error(
+                    "%sHiCache storage %s calls are refused until one of the %d "
+                    "hung %s calls returns: the storage backend is unhealthy and "
+                    "every %s call is now a miss",
+                    self._log_prefix(),
+                    kind.value,
+                    pending_orphans,
+                    kind.value,
+                    kind.value,
+                )
+            return miss()
+        try:
+            result = self._wait(future, timeout)
+        except _GuardTimeout:
+            self._orphan(kind, lane, worker, future, spans, op, started_at)
+            self._warn(
+                lane,
+                "HiCache storage %s call %s did not return within %.1fs (%d keys); "
+                "published as a miss, the call keeps running on an orphaned "
+                "worker (%d orphaned %s calls pending)",
+                kind.value,
+                op,
+                time.monotonic() - started_at,
+                num_keys,
+                len(lane.orphans),
+                kind.value,
+            )
+            return miss()
+        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - every backend failure is a miss
+            with self._lock:
+                lane.busy = False
+                lane.errors += 1
+            self._warn(
+                lane,
+                "HiCache storage %s call %s failed (%d keys): %r; published as a miss",
+                kind.value,
+                op,
+                num_keys,
+                error,
+                exc_info=True,
+            )
+            return miss()
+        with self._lock:
+            lane.busy = False
+        return result
+
+    def _wait(self, future: concurrent.futures.Future, timeout: float):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        while True:
+            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+            if remaining <= 0:
+                # A call that completed between the last poll and this check is
+                # still orphaned and reported as a miss (its pins are released
+                # by the done callback at once): a late result is never trusted.
+                raise _GuardTimeout()
+            try:
+                return future.result(timeout=min(remaining, _STOP_POLL_INTERVAL_S))
+            except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
+                if future.done():
+                    # The backend raised a TimeoutError of its own: a failure,
+                    # not our deadline (the two are the same class on 3.11+).
+                    return future.result()
+                if self._stop_event is not None and self._stop_event.is_set():
+                    deadline = min(deadline, time.monotonic() + _STOP_GRACE_S)
+
+    def _orphan(
+        self,
+        kind: StorageCallKind,
+        lane: _Lane,
+        worker: _Worker,
+        future: concurrent.futures.Future,
+        spans: Optional[Callable[[], Sequence[HostSpan]]],
+        op: str,
+        started_at: float,
+    ) -> None:
+        # Retire the worker and free the lane before pinning: a failure while
+        # pinning must not leave the lane busy, which would turn every later
+        # call of this kind into the one-caller error.
+        orphan = _Orphan(kind, (), op, started_at)
+        with self._lock:
+            lane.busy = False
+            lane.timeouts += 1
+            worker.orphaned = True
+            lane.worker = None
+            # Wakes the worker if the call already finished and it is idle.
+            worker.inbox.put(None)
+            orphan_id = lane.next_orphan_id
+            lane.next_orphan_id += 1
+            lane.orphans[orphan_id] = orphan
+        held: list[HostSpan] = []

+        try:
+            for span in spans() if spans is not None else ():

+                span.pool.quarantine(span.indices)
+                held.append(span)
+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an unprotected orphan is loud, not fatal

+                "%sHiCache storage %s call %s timed out but its host span could "
+                "not be quarantined (%s, %d spans pinned): the orphaned call may "
+                "still write slots that are handed out again",
+                self._log_prefix(),
+                kind.value,
+                op,
+                pool_name,
+                len(held),
+            )
+        with self._lock:
+            orphan.spans = tuple(held)
+        future.add_done_callback(
+            lambda done: self._orphan_returned(lane, orphan_id, done)
+        )
+
+    def _orphan_returned(
+        self, lane: _Lane, orphan_id: int, future: concurrent.futures.Future
+    ) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            orphan = lane.orphans[orphan_id]
+            released: list[HostSpan] = []
+            try:
+                for span in orphan.spans:
+                    span.pool.release_quarantine(span.indices)
+                    released.append(span)
+            finally:
+                if len(released) == len(orphan.spans):
+                    del lane.orphans[orphan_id]
+                else:
+                    # A failed release keeps the orphan, and its remaining
+                    # spans pinned, visible instead of silently dropping them.
+                    orphan.spans = tuple(
+                        span for span in orphan.spans if span not in released
+                    )

+                lane.refusing = False
+        error = future.exception()
+        logger.warning(
+            "%sHiCache storage %s call %s orphaned by its deadline returned after "
+            "%.1fs (%s); its host span is released%s",
+            self._log_prefix(),
+            orphan.kind.value,
+            orphan.op,
+            time.monotonic() - orphan.started_at,
+            "ok" if error is None else repr(error),
+            f", {orphan.kind.value} calls are served again" if recovered else "",
+        )
+
+    def _log_prefix(self) -> str:
+        return f"[{self._label}] " if self._label else ""
+
+    def _warn(self, lane: _Lane, message: str, *args, exc_info: bool = False) -> None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        with self._lock:
+            if now - lane.last_warn_at < _WARN_INTERVAL_S:
+                lane.suppressed_warnings += 1
+                return
+            suppressed = lane.suppressed_warnings
+            lane.suppressed_warnings = 0
+            lane.last_warn_at = now
+        if suppressed:
+            message += " (%d similar warnings suppressed)"
+            args = (*args, suppressed)

+class _Backend:

+    block on ``gate`` or raise."""

+    def __init__(self, hang=(), fail=(), error=RuntimeError):
+        self.hang, self.fail, self.error = set(hang), set(fail), error
+        self.calls = defaultdict(int)

+        self.gate = threading.Event()
+        self.hung = threading.Event()

+    def _enter(self, method):
+        index = self.calls[method]
+        self.calls[method] += 1
+        self.threads[method].append(threading.current_thread().name)
+        if (method, index) in self.hang:
+            self.hung.set()
+            self.gate.wait()
+        if (method, index) in self.fail:
+            raise self.error(f"injected {method} #{index}")

+        self._enter("batch_exists")
+        return len(keys)

+    def batch_get_v1(self, keys, host_indices, extra_info=None):

+def _prefetch_op(kind, rid, pool, num_pages=2):
+    tokens = list(range(num_pages * PAGE_SIZE))
+    if kind == "base":
+        op = BasePrefetchOp(rid, tokens)
+    else:
+        op = HybridPrefetchOp(CacheRequestHandle(rid, 0), tokens)
+    op.hash_value = [f"{rid}-{i}" for i in range(num_pages)]
+    op.host_indices = pool.alloc(num_pages * PAGE_SIZE)
+    return op
+
+
+def _backup_op(pool, num_pages=2):
+    host_indices = pool.alloc(num_pages * PAGE_SIZE)
+    return BaseStorageOp(
+        host_indices,
+        list(range(num_pages * PAGE_SIZE)),
+        hash_value=[f"b{i}" for i in range(num_pages)],
+    )

+def _start(target, name):
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=target, daemon=True, name=name)
+    thread.start()
+    return thread
+
+
+def _stop(cc, thread, queue):
+    cc.storage_stop_event.set()
+    queue.put(None)
+    thread.join(5)
+
+
+def _drain(queue, want, budget_s=5.0):
+    got = []
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + budget_s
+    while len(got) < want and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            got.append(queue.get(timeout=0.1))
+        except Empty:
+            continue
+    return got
+
+
+def _orphans(cc, kind):
+    return cc.storage_call_guard.take_stats().orphaned[kind]
+
+
+def _wait_until(predicate, budget_s=5.0):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + budget_s
+    while not predicate():
+        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
+            return False
+        time.sleep(0.01)
+    return True
+
+
+def _allocatable(pool):
+    """Every slot the pool is still willing to hand out."""
+    slots = []
+    while True:
+        got = pool.alloc(PAGE_SIZE)
+        if got is None:
+            break
+        slots.extend(got.tolist())
+    return sorted(slots)

+        self.assertTrue(_wait_until(lambda: _orphans(cc, "get") == 0))
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE - len(failed.host_indices))
+        pool.free(failed.host_indices)
+        served = _prefetch_op("base", "served", pool)
+        cc.prefetch_buffer.put(served)
+        acks = _drain(cc.prefetch_sync_queue, 2)
+        self.assertEqual([ack.completed_tokens for ack in acks], [2 * PAGE_SIZE, None])
+        self.assertTrue(worker.is_alive())
+        _stop(cc, worker, cc.prefetch_buffer)
+
+    def test_kv_miss_skips_the_derived_sidecar_read(self):
+        """A batch whose KV read came back empty is a miss whatever its
+        KV-derived sidecar holds; issuing the sidecar read anyway would cost a
+        second bound on a hung backend and pin the same span twice."""
+        backend = _Backend(fail={("batch_get_v1", 0)})
+        cc, pool = _controller("base", backend)
+        op = _prefetch_op("base", "op", pool)
+        derived = [PoolTransfer(name=PoolName.INDEXER, indices_from_pool=PoolName.KV)]
+        hits = cc._page_transfer_kv_batch(
+            op, op.hash_value, op.host_indices, HiCacheStorageExtraInfo(), derived
+        )
+        self.assertEqual((hits, backend.calls["batch_get_v2"]), (0, 0))
+        backend = _Backend()
+        cc.storage_backend = backend
+        hits = cc._page_transfer_kv_batch(
+            op, op.hash_value, op.host_indices, HiCacheStorageExtraInfo(), derived
+        )
+        self.assertEqual((hits, backend.calls["batch_get_v2"]), (len(op.hash_value), 1))
+
+    def test_hung_sidecar_read_acks_zero_pool_hits_and_pins_the_side_pool(self):
+        """The hybrid sidecar read must still emit its pool_hits ack (the peer
+        ranks reduce it) with 0 for the timed-out pool, and the side pool's
+        own span stays quarantined."""
+        swa_pool = LogicalHostPool(size=POOL_SIZE, page_size=PAGE_SIZE)
+        backend = _Backend(hang={("batch_get_v2", 0)})
+        cc, pool = _controller("hybrid", backend, swa_pool=swa_pool)
+        op = _prefetch_op("hybrid", "swa", pool)
+        swa = PoolTransfer(
+            name=PoolName.SWA,
+            host_indices=swa_pool.alloc(2 * PAGE_SIZE),
+            keys=op.hash_value,
+        )
+        op.pool_transfers = [swa]
+        cc._page_transfer_sidecar(op, kv_completed_pages=len(op.hash_value))
+        ack = cc.prefetch_sync_queue.get_nowait()
+        self.assertEqual(ack.pool_hits, {PoolName.SWA: 0})
+        swa_pool.free(swa.host_indices)
+        self.assertEqual(swa_pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE - len(swa.host_indices))
+        backend.gate.set()
+        self.assertTrue(_wait_until(lambda: _orphans(cc, "get") == 0))
+        self.assertEqual(swa_pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE)
+
+    def test_hung_backup_acks_zero_tokens_and_pins_its_source_span(self):
+        """A timed-out write acks 0 tokens (count-stable for the peers) and
+        its source span cannot be reused while the write may still read it."""
+        backend = _Backend(hang={("batch_set_v1", 0)})
+        cc, pool = _controller("base", backend)
+        worker = _start(cc.backup_thread_func, "backup")
+        hung = _backup_op(pool)
+        cc.backup_queue.put(hung)
+        (acked,) = _drain(cc.ack_backup_queue, 1)
+        self.assertIs(acked, hung)
+        self.assertEqual(hung.completed_tokens, 0)
+        pool.free(hung.host_indices)
+        self.assertFalse(set(hung.host_indices.tolist()) & set(_allocatable(pool)))
+        backend.gate.set()
+        self.assertTrue(_wait_until(lambda: _orphans(cc, "set") == 0))
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), len(hung.host_indices))
+        self.assertTrue(worker.is_alive())
+        _stop(cc, worker, cc.backup_queue)
+
+    def test_stop_request_drains_queued_calls_without_new_waits(self):
+        """Once the stop event is set, the call in flight gets one grace period
+        and every call queued behind it is published as a miss immediately, so
+        a reset's thread join cannot be exceeded by a hung backend."""
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(storage_call_guard_module, "_STOP_GRACE_S", 0.2)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+        backend = _Backend(hang={("batch_exists", 0)})
+        cc, pool = _controller(
+            "base", backend, StorageCallTimeouts(query_s=30, get_s=30, set_s=30)
+        )
+        worker = _start(cc.prefetch_thread_func, "query")
+        ops = [_prefetch_op("base", f"op{i}", pool) for i in range(3)]
+        for op in ops:
+            op.host_indices = None
+            cc.prefetch_queue.put(op)
+        self.assertTrue(backend.hung.wait(5))
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        _stop(cc, worker, cc.prefetch_queue)
+        self.assertFalse(worker.is_alive())
+        self.assertLess(time.monotonic() - started, 2.0)
+        published = _drain(cc.prefetch_hit_queue, 3, budget_s=1.0)
+        self.assertEqual([op.storage_hit_count for op in published], [0, 0, 0])
+        stats = cc.storage_call_guard.take_stats()
+        self.assertEqual((stats.timeouts["query"], stats.orphaned["query"]), (1, 1))
+        self.assertEqual(backend.calls["batch_exists"], 1)
+        backend.gate.set()
+

+class _SlotPool(HostKVCache):
+    def get_size_per_token(self):
+        return 1

+    def init_kv_buffer(self):

+class TestHostSlotQuarantine(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_quarantined_slots_survive_free_and_clear_until_released(self):
+        """The allocator contract behind the guard: a quarantined slot is not
+        allocatable after its owner frees it or after a pool-wide clear, and
+        comes back exactly once when released."""
+        pool = _SlotPool(
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device_capacity_tokens=8,
+            size_per_token=1,
+            start_layer=0,
+            end_layer=1,
+            host_to_device_ratio=1.0,
+            host_size=0,
+            page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+            layout="layer_first",
+            pin_memory=False,
+            device="cpu",
+            is_dummy=True,
+        )
+        size = pool.available_size()
+        span = pool.alloc(2 * PAGE_SIZE)
+        pool.quarantine(span)
+        pool.free(span)
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), size - len(span))
+        self.assertFalse(set(span.tolist()) & set(_allocatable(pool)))
+        pool.clear()
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), size - len(span))
+        pool.release_quarantine(span)
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), size)
+        self.assertEqual(len(_allocatable(pool)), size)
+
+    def test_overlapping_pins_are_counted(self):
+        """Two calls can pin the same slots (a KV read and its sidecar read,
+        a whole-operation write over its per-batch writes); the first one to
+        return must not unprotect the slots the other still uses."""
+        pool = LogicalHostPool(size=POOL_SIZE, page_size=PAGE_SIZE)
+        span = pool.alloc(2 * PAGE_SIZE)
+        pool.quarantine(span)
+        pool.quarantine(span[:PAGE_SIZE])
+        pool.free(span)
+        pool.release_quarantine(span)
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE - PAGE_SIZE)
+        self.assertFalse(set(span[:PAGE_SIZE].tolist()) & set(_allocatable(pool)))
+        pool.clear()
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE - PAGE_SIZE)
+        pool.release_quarantine(span[:PAGE_SIZE])
+        self.assertEqual(pool.available_size(), POOL_SIZE)
+        pool.release_quarantine(span)
+        self.assertEqual(len(_allocatable(pool)), POOL_SIZE)
+
+    def test_unified_page_envelope_pool_pins_pages_and_bounds_clear(self):
+        """The shared page-envelope backing keeps a freed quarantined page out
+        of its free list until released, and a clear that finds an orphaned
+        call still holding the layout lease fails loudly instead of blocking
+        the scheduler thread forever."""
+        bundle = init_unified_swa_pools(
+            device="cpu",
+            kv_cache_dtype=torch.float16,
+            head_num=2,
+            head_dim=4,
+            v_head_dim=4,
+            swa_head_num=2,
+            swa_head_dim=4,
+            swa_v_head_dim=4,
+            page_size=4,
+            start_layer=0,
+            end_layer=4,
+            swa_attention_layer_ids=[3],
+            full_attention_layer_ids=[0, 1, 2],
+            total_bytes=4096,
+            enable_memory_saver=False,
+            need_sort=False,
+            lazy_compaction=True,
+        )
+        device_pool = bundle.token_to_kv_pool
+        full, swa = UnifiedPageEnvelopeHostPool.build_hybrid_swa_pool_pair(
+            device_pools=(device_pool.full_kv_pool, device_pool.swa_kv_pool),
+            host_to_device_ratio=1.0,
+            host_size=0,
+            page_size=device_pool.page_size,
+            layout="layer_first",
+            pin_memory=False,
+            allocator_type="default",
+        )
+        self.addCleanup(full.destroy)
+        self.addCleanup(swa.destroy)
+        size = full.available_size()
+        page = full.alloc(full.page_size)
+        full.quarantine(page)
+        full.free(page)
+        self.assertEqual(full.available_size(), size - full.page_size)
+        full.release_quarantine(page)
+        self.assertEqual(full.available_size(), size)
+
+        patcher = mock.patch(
+            "sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.unified._CLEAR_LEASE_WAIT_S", 0.2
+        )
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+        leased = threading.Event()
+        release = threading.Event()
+
+        def hold_lease():
+            with full._shared_backing.layout_lease():
+                leased.set()
+                release.wait()
+
+        orphan = threading.Thread(target=hold_lease, daemon=True)
+        orphan.start()
+        self.assertTrue(leased.wait(5))
+        try:
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "still leased"):
+                full.clear()
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+            orphan.join(5)
+        full.clear()
+        self.assertEqual(full.available_size(), size)
+

+    unittest.main()
